event_peak._note: Bridge Street crest from the storm total and the wetness index at onset. Fitted on a winter whose highest crest was 7.38 ft; above that it is extrapolation.

sump_inflow._note: Peak 15-minute inflow (GPM) from the heaviest 10 minutes of rain and wetness. Last winter's max was 42.65 GPM; the run-level model under-reads the worst single runs by about 2x (report sec. 3), so the planner shows a 2x tail band.

thresholds._note: rate = station rain in the 10 min ending 5 min after the run starts, in/hr. Continuous running never observed.

tail._note: fit on runs with stress >= 0.3 only; the worst-run estimate in the planner

sump_stress_run.window: 10 min ending 5 min after the run start
sump_stress_run._note: stress = 1 - 14/run_s = Qin/Qp per run, from the 10 min of rain ending 5 min AFTER the run starts (the pit answers within minutes; a window ending at the start misses the burst). 'tail' is the same fit on stressed runs only, used for the worst-run estimate.

baseflow_to_api._note: API implied by Ross baseflow on rain-free bins; a cross-check and the fallback when the station history is unavailable.

timing._note: median across storms >= 0.5 in, heaviest hour of rain to Bridge Street crest / peak inflow

pump._note: run_s = V/(Qp-Qin); V = 14 s x Qp. Float travel is assumed, not measured (README).

observed_maxima._note: largest values the models have seen; beyond them the planner flags extrapolation

ross_to_bridge._note: Peak-to-peak fit across 24 storms, R2 0.9965, residual sd 0.0967 ft. Ross (USGS 11460000) is real-time and reliable; Bridge Street's own gauge is event-based and sparse. The notify line sits INSIDE the fitted range, the flood lines do not.

creek_predictor._note: Layer 3A, Bridge Street stage on the rising limb only (n=349 observed readings). Used by the Act tier: feed r6h_in = observed last-6h rain + bias-corrected next-6h QPF, and api = current antecedent index. Season-to-date was dropped - it added +0.005 R2 across every layer tested.

tiers._note: Rebuilt 2026-09-08 from the winter 2025-26 replay. Ordered quiet < watch < prepare < act < emergency; the highest satisfied rule wins. 'ross_ft' is USGS 11460000 stage, 'bridge_ft' is San Anselmo at Bridge St, 'run_s' is a single primary-pump run length. QPF terms are already bias-corrected by qpf_bias.

act._escalation_note: The bare 3-increasing-runs rule fires on 2.6% of all runs (94 triggers, 21 days) and 78 of those 94 land on runs still under 25 s - a 62% false-alarm rate at Act. Requiring the third run to be at least 25 s cuts it to 16 triggers on 8 days while keeping every real storm.

tiers._sump_rate_note: Rain rate over the 10 minutes ending 5 min after a run starts (station gauge). From 3,630 runs Sep 2025-Jun 2026 (stress_model.py rate_bins): below 1.0 in/hr the longest run ever was 33 s; 1.0-1.25 in/hr runs stretch to ~30 s; from 1.25 in/hr up half the runs pass 35 s and one in eight passes 93 s. A run that never ends was never observed; the fitted model puts it near 2.1-2.7 in/hr sustained over 10 min, and the 134 s outlier came inside a 2.4 in/hr five-minute burst. 2.2 is the 95% worst-run edge at index 3.

qpf_bias._note: Open-Meteo runs dry here. Measured against station totals over Nov 2025-Apr 2026: day-ahead QPF captured 75.5% of observed rain, 3-day lead 49.6%, and the five wettest events were under-forecast 41% and 68%. Every QPF used in a rule is multiplied by these before comparison.
qpf_bias._how_applied: forecast.py multiplies each forecast hour by a factor of its lead time: lead_24h for the first 24 h, a straight line from lead_24h at 24 h to lead_72h at 72 h, and lead_72h beyond.

wetness._note: Ground wetness index. The antecedent precipitation index (API, 0.9/day decay) is the term both creek models were fitted on, so it IS the index; wetness_pct rescales it against saturated_api_in (the API when the Jan 2026 storm began, the wettest start last winter) for a 0-100 reading. USGS Ross baseflow is the cross-check and the fallback when the station history is unavailable.

planner._note: Storm-timing assumptions used by planner.html. lag_peak_rain_to_crest_h is the median lag from the heaviest hour of rain to the Bridge Street crest across last winter's storms (events.csv).

checklist.task: Clear gutters, downspouts and the north-side yard drain
Test primary pump; confirm backup pump float lifts and runs
Charge phones and lights; check the Tesla backup circuit
Move cars off the low side of Woodland
Lift basement storage off the floor; roll up rugs
Stage sandbags and barrier boards on the north side
Deploy north-side barriers (2005 water came from the north, not the sump)
Walk the creek at Bridge St; compare the gauge to the Town stage lines
Shut off power to basement outlets below 12 in; move to the upper floor

planner._peak_24h_note: For a 48-h storm the heaviest 24 h held 75-99% of the total last winter (events.csv); 0.8 converts the 48-h slider to the 24-h quantity the Prepare rule was written for.
